Class MicronautRunnerJar

java.lang.Object
org.gradle.api.internal.AbstractTask
org.gradle.api.DefaultTask
io.micronaut.runner.gradle.MicronautRunnerJar
All Implemented Interfaces:
Comparable<org.gradle.api.Task>, org.gradle.api.internal.DynamicObjectAware, org.gradle.api.internal.TaskInternal, org.gradle.api.Named, org.gradle.api.plugins.ExtensionAware, org.gradle.api.Task, org.gradle.util.Configurable<org.gradle.api.Task>
@CacheableTask public abstract class MicronautRunnerJar extends org.gradle.api.DefaultTask
Packages the application and its dependencies into a runner jar.

The plugin takes the task's inputs from the project: conventions for its properties, and the jar task's manifest configuration for the application's own manifest attributes. The task therefore normally needs no configuration at all. See the plugin documentation for the properties worth overriding.

The task is wiring: it hands the project's facts and the options the build sets to the packaging library, which owns every option's default, parsing and validation. A typed option has a property here; every option, typed or not, can also be set by name through getOptions(). Each option property takes the MicronautRunnerExtension's value as its convention, so a value set here wins for this task only. The archive is named as an archive task names it, from getArchiveBaseName(), getArchiveVersion(), getArchiveClassifier() and getDestinationDirectory().

Since:
1.0

    • getApplicationJar

      @InputFile @Optional @PathSensitive(NONE) public abstract org.gradle.api.file.RegularFileProperty getApplicationJar()
      An explicit override: a jar whose manifest supplies the application's own manifest attributes, for a manifest that the jar task's configuration cannot describe. It has no default.

      Without it, the six Implementation-* and Specification-* attributes, Sealed and the package sections come from the jar task's manifest configuration, including manifest.from(...) merges, and this task does not build the thin JAR. When attributes are added in the jar task's doFirst or doLast, or merged from a file that another task generates, set it to tasks.named('jar').flatMap { it.archiveFile }.

      Returns:
      the jar whose manifest supplies the application's attributes

    • getInheritedManifest

      @Internal public @Nullable org.gradle.api.java.archives.Manifest getInheritedManifest()
      The manifest configuration the application's own manifest attributes are taken from; the plugin sets the jar task's. It is read when this task executes, not when it is configured, so an attribute whose value is a provider, or a merged manifest file, is read as it is then. Only the attributes the archive carries are inputs: see getInheritedManifestAttributes().
      Returns:
      the manifest configuration, or null when none was set

    • getInheritedManifestAttributes

      @Input public SortedMap<String,String> getInheritedManifestAttributes()
      What the packaging library reads from the inherited manifest, as ApplicationManifest.filter(Map, Map) keeps it: the six Specification-* and Implementation-* attributes and Sealed, keyed by Name in the main section and by <section>Name in a package section, whose name ends in /. Every other attribute and section is left out, so it cannot invalidate the archive.

      Empty when there is no inherited manifest, or when getApplicationJar() overrides it.

      Returns:
      the consumed attributes, sorted by key

    • getClasspath

      @InputFiles @PathSensitive(NAME_ONLY) public abstract org.gradle.api.file.ConfigurableFileCollection getClasspath()
      The dependencies, in runtime classpath resolution order.

      This is deliberately not annotated @Classpath: that normalisation ignores the order of a jar's entries and their timestamps, which is exactly what PRESERVE compression reproduces byte for byte. File names matter too, because a dependency keeps its file name inside the archive.

      Returns:
      the dependency files

    • getDependencyInputs

      public List<MicronautRunnerJar.DependencyInput> getDependencyInputs()
      The ordered, relocatable identity of every dependency used to build the archive.

      The file collection above retains task dependency inference. This nested sequence adds the ordering Gradle's file collection snapshot does not retain and pairs each position with its file name, coordinates and raw bytes. Path sensitivity is deliberately NONE: moving an otherwise identical project must not change its cache key.

      Returns:
      dependency inputs in runtime classpath order

    • getOptions

      @Input public abstract org.gradle.api.provider.MapProperty<String,String> getOptions()
      Packaging options by name, for the options that have no typed property here. Each value uses the grammar RunnerJarOption documents, and the packaging library parses and validates it; an unknown name fails the task. An entry is applied after the typed properties, so it wins over a typed property of the same option. The plugin sets the extension's value as the convention.
      Returns:
      the options by name
